items.bewering: In graad 5 het jy geleer dat 'n voedselketting in 'n ry wys wie vir wie eet.
items.bron: CAPS NST Gr 4-6 lists 'Food chains' under Grade 5 Term 1 Life and Living (education.gov.za CAPS Intermediate Phase page, and curriculum listings at twinkl.co.za). A food chain showing who eats whom is standard (Khan Academy, 'Food chains and food webs').

items.bewering: 'n Ekostelsel het egter baie sulke kettings op dieselfde plek. Die kettings deel plante en diere en haak daarom by mekaar in. Saam vorm hulle 'n voedselweb. 'n Voedselweb wys die kosverhoudings tussen die lewende dinge in een ekostelsel.
items.bron: Khan Academy, 'Food chains and food webs'; CK-12 Middle School Life Science 12.18 'Food webs': a food web is the interconnected food chains of an ecosystem.

items.bewering: Die beeld van kettings wat by mekaar inhaak en 'n web vorm (die lestitel en die hele blokreeks)
items.bron: The mapping holds: chains sharing an organism join at that node, which is exactly how a food web is built (Khan Academy; CK-12). A learner reasoning further (one organism in several chains; removing one link affects several chains) is led correctly.

items.bewering: Die meeste diere eet meer as een soort kos. Baie diere word ook deur meer as een soort dier geëet.
items.bron: Generalist feeding is the norm in food-web ecology; generalist predators switch between prey and form key nodes of food webs (Scientific Reports 2018, 'High redundancy as well as complementary prey choice characterize generalist predator food webs'). The quantifiers 'die meeste' and 'baie' are appropriately narrow.

items.bewering: 'n Springbok vreet gras en die blare van bossies.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Springbok' and ScienceDirect (springbok dietary proxies): springbok are mixed feeders, grazing young grass and browsing shrubs and succulents.

items.bewering: 'n Jagluiperd vang springbokke.
items.bron: SeaWorld/United Parks 'Cheetah diet' and IZW Cheetah Research Project: cheetahs prey on gazelles, springbok and other small-to-medium antelope.

items.bewering: 'n Sprinkaan vreet gras en 'n sekretarisvoël vang sprinkane.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Graminivore' (many Acrididae grasshoppers feed mainly on grasses); SANBI 'Secretarybird' and Britannica 'Secretary bird': most of its diet is large insects, especially grasshoppers and locusts.

items.bewering: 'n Bobbejaan eet gras en sade, maar hy vang ook sprinkane.
items.bron: SANBI 'Chacma baboon'; Africa Geographic 'Chacma baboon': diet includes grass, seeds, fruit, bulbs and insects; baboons actively pursue grasshoppers.

items.bewering: Die sprinkaan is dus in twee kettings: een eindig by die voël en een by die bobbejaan. Daar kruis die kettings en so word hulle 'n web.
items.bron: Follows from the feeding links confirmed above (SANBI secretarybird and chacma baboon pages); a shared organism joining two chains is the definition of a web node (Khan Academy).

items.bewering: Die meeste van hierdie diere eet ook dinge wat nie hier genoem word nie.
items.bron: SANBI secretarybird (rodents, reptiles, snakes, birds), SANBI chacma baboon (fruit, bulbs, rodents, eggs), springbok succulents and forbs (Wikipedia), cheetah other antelope and hares (SeaWorld).

items.bewering: In 'n getekende web wys elke pyl van die kos na die eter. Die pyl loop dus van die gras na die springbok en nie andersom nie. Dit wys waarheen die kos gaan.
items.bron: CK-12 Flexi 'The arrows in a food chain represent the direction of the energy flow'; Khan Academy 'Food chains and food webs': arrows point from the organism eaten to the organism that eats it.

items.bewering: Elke ketting in hierdie web begin by 'n plant soos gras of bossies. 'n Plant maak sy eie kos en daarom noem ons hom 'n produsent. Hy maak die kos vir sy eie gebruik.
items.bron: Every chain in the web described begins at grass, bush leaves or seeds. Producers make their own food by photosynthesis (Khan Academy, 'Producers and consumers'; Lumen Biology for Majors II).

items.bewering: 'n Dier kry daardie kos deur die plant te eet of deur 'n dier te eet wat plante geëet het.
items.bron: SANBI 'Secretarybird' (snakes, rodents, other reptiles in diet); Khan Academy 'Food chains and food webs' (tertiary consumers eat secondary consumers). The sentence names only two routes, and the lesson's own later example breaks it: in 'As een kossoort wegval' the secretary bird switches to snakes, and a snake eats other animals (rodents, frogs, lizards), not plants. So the secretary bird gets the plant's food through a longer chain that this sentence excludes.
items.regstelling: Keep the claim but stop it closing the list at two steps: an animal gets that food by eating the plant, or by eating an animal that ate plants, or an animal that ate such an animal, and so on further along the chain. Any wording that does not imply the food can only pass through one animal before the eater is correct.

items.bewering: Jy het in graad 5 geleer dat baie van die produsente in die see alge is.
items.bron: The science is sound: microscopic algae (phytoplankton) and seaweeds are the ocean's main producers (WHOI 'Phytoplankton - A Simple Guide'; Wikipedia 'Marine primary production'; photosynthetic bacteria also contribute a large share, so 'baie' rather than 'al' is right). What could not be settled is the back-reference: no CAPS text reachable online confirms that Grade 5 teaches algae as sea producers, and the only other hits were commercial worksheet sites. A person must confirm that Wolkskool's own Grade 5 food-chain lesson says this; if it does not, the sentence should not claim the learner already learned it.

items.bewering: Die diere in die web is die verbruikers. Hulle kan nie self kos maak nie en kry dit deur plante of ander diere te eet.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Consumer (food chain)'; Khan Academy 'Producers and consumers'.

items.bewering: Die springbok en die sprinkaan vreet net plante en is dus herbivore.
items.bron: Springbok: mixed grazer-browser, plant diet only (Wikipedia 'Springbok'). Grass-feeding grasshoppers (Acrididae) are herbivores (Wikipedia 'Graminivore').

items.bewering: Die jagluiperd en die sekretarisvoël eet net ander diere en is karnivore.
items.bron: Cheetah is an obligate carnivore (SeaWorld/United Parks 'Cheetah diet'); secretarybird diet is entirely animal prey (SANBI 'Secretarybird'; Britannica). 'net' is true for these two specific animals.

items.bewering: Die bobbejaan eet plante sowel as diere en is 'n omnivoor.
items.bron: SANBI 'Chacma baboon'; Africa Geographic: chacma baboons are omnivorous.

items.bewering: Dooie blare onder 'n boom word bruin en sag en is na 'n ruk weg. 'n Omgevalle stomp word mettertyd so sag dat hy in jou hand verkrummel. Dit is veral die werk van die ontbinders. Hulle breek dooie plante en diere af.
items.bron: PMC12477604 (litter decomposition is primarily driven by microbes); RHS 'Saprotrophic fungi' (wood-decay fungi break down cellulose and lignin; brown rot leaves wood crumbly); National Geographic Education 'Decomposers'. 'veral' leaves room for the part played by earthworms, termites and other animals that feed on dead matter.

items.bewering: Baie ontbinders is mikro-organismes wat jy net deur 'n mikroskoop kan sien.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Saprotrophic bacteria'; Mosaic Crop Nutrition 'Beyond bacteria': bacteria and microscopic fungi are the main decomposers.

items.bewering: Party swamme soos sampioene is ook ontbinders en hulle kan jy wel sien.
items.bron: RHS 'Saprotrophic fungi': saprotrophic fungi are the largest group and produce visible fruiting bodies such as mushrooms and brackets. 'Party' is correctly narrow, since some mushroom-forming fungi are mycorrhizal or parasitic rather than decomposers.

items.bewering: Wanneer ontbinders 'n dooie blaar afbreek, gaan voedingstowwe uit die blaar in die grond in. 'n Plant neem hulle deur sy wortels op en gebruik hulle om te groei.
items.bron: FAO 'Organic matter decomposition and the soil food web' (a0100e05); Wikipedia 'Decomposer': decomposition releases nitrogen, phosphorus and other nutrients in forms plant roots take up.

items.bewering: Hierdie voedingstowwe is nie die plant se kos nie. Die plant maak sy kos steeds self, maar sonder hierdie stowwe groei hy swak.
items.bron: Mineral nutrients are needed for growth and function but the plant's food (sugars) comes from photosynthesis (FAO a0100e05; Encyclopedia.com 'Decomposers'). This correctly avoids the common misconception that plants get food from the soil.

items.bewering: 'n Springbok wat die gras vreet, kry die voedingstowwe ook in sy lyf. Na die springbok se dood breek ontbinders af wat van hom oorbly. So gaan dieselfde stowwe terug na die grond en weer deur die web.
items.bron: Trends in Microbiology 2024 'From carrion to soil: microbial recycling of animal carcasses'; African Journal of Plant and Soil 2024 on wildebeest carcass decomposition raising grassland soil nutrients.

items.bewering: Stel jou voor die sprinkane in die grasveld word baie min. Die bobbejaan kan dikwels meer gras en sade eet. Die sekretarisvoël kan ander diere soos slange vang.
items.bron: SANBI 'Chacma baboon' (opportunistic omnivore that changes its diet with what is available); SANBI 'Secretarybird' and Britannica (snakes, rodents and reptiles are part of its prey).

items.bewering: 'n Dier wat net een soort kos eet, kom in groter moeilikheid as sy een kos wegval.
items.bron: ScienceDirect 'Generalist predators, interaction strength and food-web stability': generalists can switch to other prey when preferred prey declines, specialists cannot.

items.bewering: Daarom hou genoeg biodiversiteit 'n ekostelsel gesond: dit hou meer paaie vir kos oop.
items.bron: Scientific Reports 2019 'Far-ranging generalist top predators enhance the stability of meta-foodwebs'; National Geographic Education 'Biodiversity'. More links (redundancy) buffer the loss of any one food. The hedge 'genoeg' keeps it from claiming more diversity always means more stability, which the research does not say.

items.bewering: voedselweb: Die voedselkettings van een ekostelsel wat by mekaar aansluit en deur mekaar loop.
items.bron: Khan Academy 'Food chains and food webs'; CK-12 12.18 'Food webs'.

items.bewering: voedselketting: 'n Ry lewende dinge wat begin by een wat sy eie kos maak. Elkeen daarna vreet die een voor hom.
items.bron: Britannica Kids 'Food chain'; Khan Academy: a food chain starts with a producer and each consumer eats the one before it. (Chains that start with dead matter exist but are not what this grade teaches, and read alone the entry is still true of every chain in the lesson.)

items.bewering: produsent: 'n Lewende ding wat sy eie kos maak, soos 'n plant.
items.bron: Khan Academy 'Producers and consumers'; WHOI 'Phytoplankton' (algae are producers too, which 'soos 'n plant' leaves open).

items.bewering: verbruiker: 'n Lewende ding wat sy kos kry deur plante of diere te eet.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Consumer (food chain)'.

items.bewering: ontbinder: 'n Lewende ding wat dooie plante en diere afbreek en voedingstowwe na die grond teruggee.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Decomposer'; National Geographic Education 'Decomposers'.

items.bewering: mikro-organisme: 'n Lewende ding wat so klein is dat 'n mens dit net deur 'n mikroskoop kan sien.
items.bron: Standard definition of a microorganism as too small to see without a microscope (Wikipedia 'Saprotrophic bacteria' context; Britannica 'microorganism').

items.bewering: voedingstof: 'n Stof wat 'n lewende ding nodig het om te groei en gesond te bly. Party voedingstowwe in kos gee ook energie.
items.bron: FAO a0100e05 (plant mineral nutrients); nutrients needed for growth and health, with carbohydrates, fats and proteins also supplying energy. 'Party' is correctly narrow.

items.bewering: herbivoor: 'n Dier wat net plante eet, soos gras, blare of vrugte.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Herbivore' ('wholly or mainly plant matter'); Lumen Biology for Majors II 'Herbivores, carnivores and omnivores'. 'net' is close enough for herbivores, whose incidental animal intake is negligible. If the writer changes 'karnivoor' (see below), this entry should be made to match so the three definitions stay parallel.

items.bewering: karnivoor: 'n Dier wat net ander diere eet.
items.bron: National Geographic Education 'Carnivore': 'an organism that eats mostly meat'; the same source notes that most carnivores are not obligate carnivores. Read alone, this glossary entry is true of the cheetah and the secretary bird but not of the category: many carnivores also eat some fruit or plant matter (for example the black-backed jackal, which eats berries).
items.regstelling: Narrow the quantifier rather than the subject: a carnivore is an animal that eats mainly other animals ('hoofsaaklik' or 'meestal' in place of 'net'). The study-text sentence about the cheetah and the secretary bird may keep 'net', because it is true of those two animals. Because this is likely a subject-wide agreed wording, the change needs to go through the shared definitions list, not this lesson alone.

items.bewering: omnivoor: 'n Dier wat plante sowel as ander diere eet.
items.bron: National Geographic 'Omnivore' encyclopedia entry; Wikipedia 'Omnivore'.

items.bewering: ekostelsel: 'n Gebied waar lewende dinge van mekaar en van die nie-lewende dinge om hulle afhang.
items.bron: National Geographic Education 'Ecosystem': a geographic area where organisms and the non-living environment work together, and every part depends on every other part.

items.bewering: biodiversiteit: Hoeveel verskillende soorte lewende dinge daar in 'n plek of op die hele Aarde is.
items.bron: National Geographic Education 'Biodiversity': the variety of life on Earth, or of the species in one region or ecosystem.

items.bewering: Superlatiewe: die les bevat geen 'eerste', 'oudste', 'grootste', 'vinnigste' of 'enigste' nie; die naaste is die hoeveelheidswoorde 'die meeste' en 'baie' in 'Hoekom dit 'n web is'.
items.bron: Every block read for superlatives. The only quantifier claims ('Die meeste diere eet meer as een soort kos'; 'Die meeste van hierdie diere eet ook dinge ...') are verified in their own items above.

opsomming: Almost everything checks out, but a person must confirm one back-reference: that learners really met sea algae as producers in Grade 5. Two claims are wrong and go to the writer: the line saying an animal gets plant food only by eating a plant or a plant-eater (the lesson's own secretary bird eating snakes breaks this), and the glossary entry defining a carnivore as eating 'only' other animals, when sources say 'mainly'.
